author: david6666666
body: Small heads-up: this flag only reaches the dense `flash_attn_func` branch here — the varlen/packed/masked paths (and `forward_xpu`/`forward_npu`) never see it. Fine for Qwen-Image (dense, unmasked), but anyone enabling `VLLM_OMNI_FA_DETERMINISTIC=1` on a model that takes a varlen/masked path would get no determinism, silently. A debug log when the flag is set on a non-dense path would make that visible.

author: david6666666
body: Nit: the comment says "Explicit config True wins", but as written `VLLM_OMNI_FA_DETERMINISTIC=1` always forces `True` over a config `False` (and can't disable an explicit `True` either). Maybe "env can only enable, never disable" reads closer to what it does.

author: fhfuih
body:
If this is after all an env var injection, what do you think if we directly read env var from attention backend's `__init__`, instead of maintaining a second variable in od_config?

If you choose to present the field in od_config, I would assume is it intended to be a user-aware toggle (instead of hidden and secretly used by CI). In this case, I think you should let CI pass an extra server_arg (to be forwarded to od_config), not setting an env var.

author: NumberWan
body: Qwen-Image uses the dense unmasked path, so the accuracy test is covered. Added a warning_once when fa_deterministic=True but the call takes piecewise / packed / masked / varlen-fallback paths, so enabling the flag on those models isn’t silent.

author: NumberWan
body: That comment is gone with the env avoided.

author: NumberWan
body: Applied with the second option. Kept fa_deterministic on OmniDiffusionConfig as a user-facing toggle and wired CLI --fa-deterministic → config; the accuracy test passes it as a server_arg. No env injection in the attention backend.
